findings.text: After Settings cancelled the panel's code and opened its own, closing the panel closed the Settings code. Now the panel stores the minted code and closes the offer only if it is still that code.
An expired code while msgblast was inactive showed an endless spinner; it now shows Show pairing code.

Chains broke at closures, blank lines and comments, and comments or strings could match; now followed and stripped, with two new tests. A large modifier closure could give a false positive (safe direction).
When a Settings code expires while msgblast is active, the panel replaces it and owns the new one.
A lock/unlock or Remote off/on cycle can re-mint a code that Settings had cancelled, without the button.
A business chat with a nil businessConversation flag but a urn:biz: handle would get the address link; spaces and SMS chats untested.
No UI test reads the removed labels; lookups use identifiers and values, which are kept.
